transcript: New York Theatre Workshop is presenting a fresh and fearless new work called Becoming Eve based on the memoir by Abby Chava Stein. Chava is a trans woman trying to reconcile her Hasidic Jewish upbringing with her trans identity. One extensive scene unfolds in the present day where she and a progressive rabbi / mentor named Jonah wrestle with an interpretation of The Torah as a way to come out to her father. This is interspersed with flashback scenes from her devout upbringing showing us how her identity has long been a point of personal confusion and conflict. It also gives us context suggesting how problematic being trans would be considered by her family and community, and therefore how high the stakes are in the present. In these flashbacks, Chava’s body is portrayed using puppetry, which is a smart theatrical device for this story as it can allude to body and gender dysphoria or the ghosts of our past selves. This is a moving and philosophical tale of religious trauma and self-discovery, and ultimately an earnest ode to self-actualization and acceptance. I attended the first preview which was a bit long for a one-act, but otherwise in very good shape, with a great leading performance by Tommy Dorfman. The scenework flows naturally but methodically, giving space for the script and ideas to take center stage — it gave me a lot to think about, and I'm grateful for that. With that, another program for my collection.
